wuresidenz.name: Würzburg Residence
wuresidenz.slogan: A prince-bishop's palace with a staircase the size of a sky.
wuresidenz.line: Its Tiepolo staircase fresco, painted in 1752-53, covers about 580 square metres under a single vault.

wufestung.name: Marienberg Fortress
wufestung.slogan: Vineyards climb the hill to the bishops' old fortress home.
wufestung.line: Würzburg's prince-bishops made this hill their permanent residence after 1253 and stayed for roughly 450 years.

wumainbruecke.name: Old Main Bridge
wumainbruecke.slogan: Twelve stone saints watch the Frankenwein flow across the Main.
wumainbruecke.line: Built between 1473 and 1543 on the site of a Romanesque bridge, it was lined with twelve Baroque statues of saints and kings around 1730.

wuveitshoechheim.name: Veitshöchheim Court Garden
wuveitshoechheim.slogan: A Rococo pleasure garden where sandstone figures crowd the hedges.
wuveitshoechheim.line: Redesigned from 1763 for Prince-Bishop Seinsheim, the garden is about 270 by 475 metres and holds some 200 sculptures.

wuschlossweikersheim.name: Weikersheim Palace
wuschlossweikersheim.slogan: A Renaissance hall of painted hunts, and a baroque garden outside.
wuschlossweikersheim.line: The Knights' Hall ceiling carries 69 painted hunting scenes by Balthasar Katzenberger, from the early 1600s, with stucco animals below.
